title: 〜にひきかえ
simpleExplanation: 〜にひきかえ sets two things side by side and stresses how different they are: "compared with A, B is completely different". It usually carries a judgement: A is good and B is bad, or the reverse. 引き換え means "exchange", so picture swapping A for B and seeing the gap.
whenUsed: Both spoken and written, somewhat formal. Very common when comparing two people (a hard-working sister and a lazy brother), two periods (last year and this year) or two situations. Because it often criticises one side, avoid it in polite conversation about the listener.
formation: 普通形 + の + にひきかえ (na-adj: 〜な + の)
Formal spelling: 〜に引き換え / 〜に引き替え

rows.label: 〜にひきかえ
cells: 兄にひきかえ弟は無口だ

rows.label: 〜に対して
cells: 兄は明るいのに対して弟は静かだ

examples.ja: 兄が社交的なのにひきかえ、弟は無口だ。
examples.reading: あにがしゃこうてきなのにひきかえ、おとうとはむくちだ。
examples.en: In contrast to the sociable older brother, the younger one is quiet.
examples.note: Two brothers, opposite personalities. The clause before にひきかえ takes の (社交的なのに).

examples.ja: 去年の暖冬にひきかえ、今年は厳しい寒さが続いている。
examples.reading: きょねんのだんとうにひきかえ、ことしはきびしいさむさがつづいている。
examples.en: Unlike last year's mild winter, this year the severe cold continues.
examples.note: Two periods contrasted: mild last year, harsh this year.

examples.ja: 彼女の努力にひきかえ、私は何もしていない。
examples.reading: かのじょのどりょくにひきかえ、わたしはなにもしていない。
examples.en: Compared to her efforts, I have done nothing.
examples.note: Self-criticism: her effort versus my inaction.

examples.ja: 昔の学生が本をよく読んだのにひきかえ、今の学生はスマホばかり見ている。
examples.reading: むかしのがくせいがほんをよくよんだのにひきかえ、いまのがくせいはスマホばかりみている。
examples.en: In contrast to students of the past, who read a lot, today's students are always looking at their phones.
examples.note: A typical complaint-style contrast; the second half is criticised.

examples.ja: 姉が几帳面なのにひきかえ、私はいい加減な性格だ。
examples.reading: あねがきちょうめんなのにひきかえ、わたしはいいかげんなせいかくだ。
examples.en: Unlike my meticulous sister, I have a careless personality.
examples.note: な-adjective + なの + にひきかえ.

similarGrammar.difference: Neutral contrast of two facts without a strong evaluation.
A comparison of degree (more, less). にひきかえ says the two are of opposite kinds.
"Even more than": a comparison of degree against a high standard, not an opposite-kind contrast.

commonMistakes.wrong: 兄が社交的にひきかえ、弟は無口だ。
commonMistakes.right: 兄が社交的なのにひきかえ、弟は無口だ。
commonMistakes.why: A clause before にひきかえ needs の (with な for na-adjectives), because ひきかえ attaches to a noun-like unit.

commonMistakes.wrong: 今日は昨日にひきかえ、少し暖かい。
commonMistakes.right: 今日は昨日に比べて、少し暖かい。
commonMistakes.why: A small difference of degree (少し) is a comparison, not a stark contrast; use に比べて.

commonMistakes.wrong: あなたにひきかえ、私は…（相手を批判する場面で）
commonMistakes.why: にひきかえ implies a judgement; using it about the listener in their presence can sound rude.

usageNotes: The two items are usually of the same category (two people, two years, two companies) so the contrast is sharp.
It often appears with 一方 or は in the second clause: AにひきかえBは.
Writers use it for rhetorical effect; it is stronger than に対して and shows the writer's opinion.
jlptTips: If the two halves are opposites (社交的 vs 無口, 暖冬 vs 厳しい寒さ) and one side is evaluated, にひきかえ is the answer.
Distractors: に比べて (degree), に対して (neutral), にもまして (more than). Look for opposite kinds rather than more/less.
In 並べ替え, the chunk before にひきかえ often ends in なの or たの.
